suggestions.expectation: brief.md is under 1,600 characters (wc -c) and states the released version v0.1.9
suggestions.reason: The skill's 'Done when' asks the executor to both post the ~1,500-char brief and answer the user's question; this run appended a 546-char follow-up question after the template block and failed on total size. Decide whether brief.md should contain only the template block (and say so in the eval prompt/output spec) or whether the answer counts toward the limit — otherwise the expectation partly measures output-file packaging rather than brief discipline. Note the template block alone was still 1621, so the failure is real either way.

suggestions.expectation: brief.md contains a line starting with 'read in full:' that names docs/OVERVIEW.md, CONTEXT.md and the newest SES file, and transcript.md shows each of those was read to its last line
suggestions.reason: 'the newest SES file' is ambiguous once the run has created SES-006; specify 'the newest pre-existing SES file (SES-005 in this fixture)'. Also, transcript.md is written by the executor, so 'transcript shows it was read to its last line' is self-reported; a grader can only cross-check claimed line ranges against wc -l. A harness-captured tool log would make this expectation genuinely discriminating.

No expectation checks that every template line label is present (Released / Unreleased on main / Parked / Findings / Open-unverified / Next / Session file / read in full). The skill says 'every line present'; a brief that dropped 'Open / unverified' or 'Parked' would still pass expectations 2 and 6 as long as the named facts appeared somewhere.

No expectation checks that the brief surfaces the unexpected checkout branch as a finding in its own right (the fixture sits on feat/session-skill, 4 commits ahead of origin/main and absent from OVERVIEW Status). This run did report it and proposed dealing with it before PLAN-001 — a good outcome the evals do not reward, and a baseline that started PLAN-001 straight from the stale branch would not be penalised.

eval_feedback.overall: Expectations are mostly discriminating and verifiable against the fixture (git state, placeholder untouched, session file content). The size limit needs a decision about whether the answer to the user's question is part of brief.md, and the read-to-EOF check leans on an executor-authored transcript.
